source.role: Exact English objectives, speaking roles, grammar examples, word anchors and Reader lines retained as provenance; Japanese learner scenes are original contextual teach-back dialogues

sourceEnglish.title: Teach a Friend How a Madrid Bar Breakfast Works
sourceEnglish.objective: Explain step by step how to order, eat and pay at a Madrid bar counter, then have a friend explain it back.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are coaching the AI, Brazilian traveler Thiago, through a Madrid bar breakfast: explain ordering, eating and paying in order with primero, luego, después, porque and por eso, then ask him to explain the routine back to you.
englishWordAnchors: the gap (free spot at the bar)
First you find a spot at the bar, and then you order.
Don't wait for a table, because almost everyone here eats breakfast standing up.
You pay at the end, so don't throw away the receipt.
One moment, please, he's still deciding.
I'll have a black coffee and some porras, please.
Afterwards, when you finish, you ask the waiter for the bill.
Okay, now you explain it to me, step by step.
Can you ring me up when you get a chance?
englishGrammarExamples: First you order at the bar, and then they serve you the coffee.
Since it's so busy, first you find a spot and then you call the waiter.
englishReading: Emma and her Brazilian friend Thiago walk into a bar in Lavapiés to have breakfast before strolling around the neighborhood.
It's really hectic, because at 9 half the neighborhood has its coffee at the bar.
Emma: First you find a spot at the bar, and then you order.
Emma: Don't wait for a table, because almost everyone here eats breakfast standing up.
Thiago finds a spot at the end of the bar and leaves his backpack on a free bar stool.
Emma: Before ordering, you look at the chalkboard menu, because that's where they write the day's prices.
The breakfast deal includes a coffee and churros for 3 euros.
Suddenly Paco, the waiter, plants himself in front of them and asks: What can I get you?
Thiago freezes, so Emma answers: One moment, please, he's still deciding.
After looking at the chalkboard again, Thiago says: I'll have a black coffee and some porras, please.
Emma orders a slice of Spanish omelette and a fresh-squeezed orange juice, and Paco serves them right away.
When Paco puts down the plates, he also puts a small receipt under Thiago's cup.
Emma: You pay at the end, so don't throw away the receipt.
Emma: Afterwards, when you finish, you ask the waiter for the bill.
Emma: If you pay by card, Paco brings you the card reader, and if you pay cash, he gives you your change.
Emma: Tipping isn't required, but if you want, you leave a few coins from your change in the tip jar.
Emma: Okay, now you explain it to me, step by step.
Thiago: First I find a spot and order, then I eat breakfast standing up, and since I pay at the end, I keep the receipt.

lessons.title: Explain this café’s breakfast routine
lessons.objective: Teach a friend this café’s sequence for finding a seat, ordering and paying, then have the friend explain it back.
lessons.focus: まず・次に・最後に order steps; ～ので gives a reason. ここでは limits a rule to this café. The English Madrid source’s standing-bar, receipt and tip customs are not presented as universal Japanese practice.
lessons.scene: A traveler coaches a friend through the routine posted at a particular café.

cards.ja: まず店の案内を見ます
cards.en: First, we look at the shop instructions

cards.ja: 次にレジで注文します
cards.en: Next, we order at the register

cards.ja: 最後に番号を呼ばれたら受け取ります
cards.en: Finally, we pick it up when our number is called

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: この店の朝食の流れを説明しますね。
reader.en: Let me explain this café’s breakfast routine.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: お願いします。どこから始めますか。
reader.en: Please do. Where do we start?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: まず、入口の案内を見て、席が空いているか確認します。
reader.en: First, check the sign at the entrance and see whether a seat is free.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 次は注文ですか。
reader.en: Is ordering next?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: はい。この店ではレジで先に注文して会計します。
reader.en: Yes. At this café, we order and pay at the register first.

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 番号札を受け取るので、なくさないでください。
reader.en: You get a numbered ticket, so please do not lose it.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 飲み物はどこで受け取りますか。
reader.en: Where do we pick up the drink?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 番号を呼ばれたらカウンターで受け取ります。
reader.en: When they call the number, we pick it up at the counter.

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: では、今度はあなたが順番を説明してみてください。
reader.en: Now please explain the steps back to me.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: まず案内を見て、次にレジで注文と会計をして、最後に番号で受け取ります。
reader.en: First I check the sign, next I order and pay at the register, and finally I pick it up by number.

speaking.opening: この店では、どこで注文しますか。
speaking.goal: Explain three steps and a reason with まず, 次に, 最後に and ～ので, then invite the learner to teach them back.
speaking.closure: Ask staff if posted instructions differ from the scene.

modes.see: Read a teach-back scene with English support.
modes.recall: Recall three steps and one reason.
modes.hear: Hear sequence connectors in a complete explanation.
modes.type: Type the register step with kana help.
modes.say: Teach the café routine and check the friend’s explanation.
modes.write: Write a three-step routine for this shop.

sourceEnglish.title: Explain Media or Entera at a Seville Tostada Bar
sourceEnglish.objective: Explain how tostadas are ordered by bread type, size and topping, and why locals choose each one.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are explaining Seville's tostada system to the AI, hostel roommate Ingrid: walk her through bread type, size and toppings and why locals choose each, using impersonal se (se pide media o entera) and si + present (si pides mollete…).
englishWordAnchors: the pork loin in lard spread
the soft inside of the bread
Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.
If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside.
If you're really hungry, order a whole one.
If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.
Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?
Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.
For me, a half with tomato and oil, please.
How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?
englishGrammarExamples: Here you order the bread first and then the topping.
If you order a pitufo, they bring you a smaller roll.
englishReading: This morning, at a tostada bar in Triana, I explain to Ingrid how tostadas are ordered in Seville.
Me: Here you order the bread first and then the topping.
Me: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.
Me: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.
Me: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside, because it has a lot of soft crumb.
Me: The Vienna roll has a thinner, crunchier crust, and a lot of people prefer it for that reason.
Me: If you order a pitufo, they bring you a smaller roll, perfect to go with a coffee.
Me: I think the house bread is a mollete, but I'm going to ask.
I say to the owner: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?
Rocío: The house bread is a Vienna roll, and the mollete is ordered separately.
Me: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.
Then I tell Ingrid that the most typical choice is grated tomato with a good drizzle of olive oil, because it is light and fresh.
Me: Manteca colorá is pork lard with paprika, and zurrapa de lomo has little pieces of pork loin in lard.
Ingrid tells me she doesn't eat pork, and I explain that cured ham is pork too.
Me: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.
Ingrid: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?
Rocío: You order it with light toasting, and we bring it out to you softer.
In the end, Ingrid orders a half with tomato and oil, lightly toasted, and Rocío leaves the salt shaker on the table for her.

lessons.title: Explain bread choices at a café
lessons.objective: Teach a friend to ask about bread size, type and toppings, using conditional Japanese and checking actual ingredients.
lessons.focus: 小さいほう・大きいほう compare sizes; ～なら introduces a condition; ～によって違います marks variation. Do not transfer Seville bread names or assert that a topping is safe for a restricted diet; ask staff about ingredients and preparation.
lessons.scene: A traveler helps a friend understand a café’s bread menu without assuming ingredients.

cards.ja: 小さいほうなら、こちらです
cards.en: If you want the smaller one, it is this one

cards.ja: 具は何が入っていますか
材料を確認していただけますか

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: パンは大きさと具を別々に選べるようです。
reader.en: It looks like you can choose the bread size and topping separately.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 小さいほうはどれですか。
reader.en: Which one is smaller?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: メニューではこちらです。でも店員さんに確認しましょう。
reader.en: The menu shows this one. But let us confirm with staff.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: こちらが小さいサイズで、あちらが大きいサイズです。
reader.en: This is the small size, and that is the large size.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 具は何を選べますか。
reader.en: Which toppings can we choose?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: バターとジャムがあります。ほかは本日のメニューをご覧ください。
reader.en: We have butter and jam. Please see today’s menu for others.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 乳製品を避けています。材料を確認できますか。
reader.en: I avoid dairy. Can you check the ingredients?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 厨房に確認してからお答えします。
reader.en: I will answer after checking with the kitchen.

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 確認できない場合は、そのパンを選ばないほうがいいですね。
reader.en: If it cannot be verified, we should not choose that bread.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: わかりました。大きさ、具、材料の順に確認します。
reader.en: Understood. I will check size, topping and ingredients in that order.

speaking.opening: パンはどうやって選びますか。
speaking.goal: Teach the friend to ask about size and toppings, use a conditional phrase, and confirm ingredients before selecting food.
speaking.closure: Do not promise a restricted-diet item is suitable without kitchen verification.

modes.see: Read a conditional menu explanation with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall size, topping and ingredient questions.
modes.hear: Hear 小さいほう and 大きいほう.
modes.type: Type a conditional size request with kana support.
modes.say: Teach a friend how to verify a bread order.
modes.write: Write a conditional menu explanation and ingredient question.

sourceEnglish.title: Coach Your Niece to Order Café de Olla Alone
sourceEnglish.objective: Coach a teenager to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, with clear tips about the hot clay cup.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are the aunt or uncle, and the AI is your 15-year-old niece Sofi: coach her to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, using commands with pronouns like pídelo, agárralo por el asa and no lo toques todavía.
englishWordAnchors: the hot chocolate made with water
Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
Greet her first and speak to her formally.
Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
englishGrammarExamples: If it's very hot, leave it on the table for a little while.
Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it.
englishReading: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.
Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.
Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.
Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.
Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.
Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.
Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.
Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.
Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.
Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.

lessons.title: Coach a teen through a hot drink order
lessons.objective: Coach a teenager to order a hot drink and bread politely, confirm the price, and handle a hot cup without touching it prematurely.
lessons.focus: 先にあいさつして and ～てください sequence polite coaching. 熱いので、持つ前に確認してください gives a reason. A hot cup can burn even if steam is less visible; never use steam disappearance as a safety test. Choose a non-coffee drink in this scenario while retaining the English café de olla scene only as source provenance.
lessons.scene: An adult coaches a teenager to order a hot cocoa and bread at a café counter.

cards.ja: 先にあいさつしてください
値段を聞いてください
熱いカップに気をつけてください
cards.en: Please be careful with the hot cup

reader.speaker: Adult
reader.ja: まず、店員さんにあいさつしてみてください。
reader.en: First, try greeting the staff member.

reader.speaker: Teen
reader.ja: おはようございます。ホットココアを一杯お願いします。
reader.en: Good morning. One hot cocoa, please.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: かしこまりました。パンもいかがですか。
reader.en: Certainly. Would you like bread too?

reader.speaker: Teen
reader.ja: はい。こちらのパンを一つお願いします。
reader.en: Yes. One of this bread, please.

reader.speaker: Adult
reader.ja: 値段も聞いてみてください。
reader.en: Please ask the price too.

reader.speaker: Teen
reader.ja: 全部でいくらですか。
reader.en: How much is it altogether?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: こちらの金額です。飲み物は熱いのでお気をつけください。
reader.en: It is this amount. Please be careful; the drink is hot.

reader.speaker: Adult
reader.ja: カップは熱いです。受け取る前に安全な持ち方を確認しましょう。
reader.en: The cup is hot. Let us check how to carry it safely before taking it.

reader.speaker: Teen
reader.ja: 少し待ってから飲みます。
reader.en: I will wait a little before drinking it.

reader.speaker: Adult
reader.ja: よくできました。私はここで待っています。
reader.en: Well done. I will wait here.

speaking.opening: 最初に何と言えばいいですか。
speaking.goal: Coach a greeting, an order, a price question and a hot-cup precaution; let the teen speak independently.
speaking.closure: Do not use a reduction in visible steam as proof the cup is safe.

modes.hear: Hear polite requests and ので in context.
modes.type: Type a price question with kana support.
modes.say: Coach the teen, then let them place the order.
